comment: The selling points of the feature catalogue. This file — not the spec set — decides what the catalogue contains: the catalogue is a pitch, not an inventory, so a capability is published only if a highlight here names its spec. Add a highlight when a capability is something you would put on a landing page; leave the basics out. `keyword` is a suggestion for the entry's bold lead and the model may improve it; `specs` are the specs whose user-visible capabilities the entry is written from, and a spec may appear in more than one highlight. `why` is for a reviewer, not for the document.

highlights.why: The app's central claim: the map, the search and the routing all work with no network.

highlights.keyword: Plan it before you set off
highlights.why: Distance, time and the whole turn list on screen before you commit to driving.
The guidance a driver actually reads: the next manoeuvre, the street, the arrival estimate.

highlights.keyword: Know which lane to be in
highlights.why: Junctions are where a navigation app earns its keep; drawn lane arrows and roundabout exits.

highlights.keyword: Off course, then back on it
highlights.why: Miss a turn and the app notices, says so and recalculates without losing the route that is still valid.
Free-text and structured search over the offline database, ranked, with history.
Category and radius search — fuel, food, charging — the thing you actually do mid-journey.
Navigate to a person's address by name, with the contacts permission asked for properly.
Groups, colours, explicit ordering, stars and markers: favourites that stay usable past twenty entries.

highlights.keyword: Tap the map to see what is there
highlights.why: A long press resolves what is under your finger and shows a structured description with a mini map.

highlights.keyword: The same app on your car screen
highlights.why: A real car app: standalone Android Automotive OS head units and Android Auto projection, one installation.
The car has its own guidance surface, and the host's rail widget and cluster can show the same manoeuvre.

highlights.keyword: Find a destination from the car
highlights.why: Search, favourites and details without touching the phone.

highlights.keyword: Send a place to the car
highlights.why: Share a location from any app, or start on the phone and continue on the car screen.

highlights.keyword: Day, night, or your own style
highlights.why: Every bundled stylesheet, day and night, chosen once and shared between phone and car.

highlights.keyword: A map that keeps up with your fingers
highlights.why: Zoom and pan stay fluid because the map is redrawn deliberately rather than on every touch.

highlights.keyword: Speed, limit and the road you are on
highlights.why: Live speed against the limit, and the street name resolved by heading rather than by proximity.

highlights.keyword: German and English, phone and car
highlights.why: Localised interface and rebuilt turn instructions, on both surfaces.
OpenStreetMap data, its attribution on the map, and a documented answer to what the app does with your location.
